evaluated.name: Stability-Weighted Intangible Intensity
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible spending is rewarded only when the firm's earnings stream is stable enough to sustain and monetize it; intensity plus low ROA volatility identifies durable intangible productivity.
evaluated.reasoning: Investors under-react to intangible investment because its payoff is uncertain, but that uncertainty is far smaller for firms whose realized ROA is highly stable across five years. Ranking intangible intensity jointly with earnings stability isolates credible, repeatable intangible capital formation rather than speculative spending spikes. Unreported R&D/advertising is economically a zero outlay, so COALESCE to zero is the correct convention.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash-Covered Innovation Intensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D intensity is credible when operating cash flow comfortably covers total liabilities; innovation financed from internal cash is durable, whereas innovation at cash-poor, liability-heavy firms is optional and easily abandoned.
evaluated.reasoning: The multiplicative form makes the payoff to intangible intensity increase in balance-sheet cash coverage, so the signal is near zero for high-R&D firms with weak cash generation and for cash-rich firms that do not innovate. Three-year smoothing of coverage removes transitory cash-flow noise and focuses on a persistent funding state. This is an explicit conditional interaction, not a standalone R&D or cash-flow effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Accrual-Backed Goodwill Overhang
evaluated.expression: MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), INDICATOR(SUB(ib, oancf), 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles (goodwill) predict poor returns specifically at firms whose earnings exceed operating cash flow, i.e., where reported profits are accrual-driven and impairment risk is unrecognized.
evaluated.reasoning: Goodwill alone is a weak, noisy predictor; its return drag concentrates in firms that simultaneously fail the cash-conversion quality test, since these are the acquirers most likely facing future write-downs and earnings reversals. The indicator switches the goodwill exposure on only in the low-quality state, creating a genuine conditional interaction rather than a single-theme goodwill effect. Firms without reported goodwill economically have zero goodwill.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Persistent Innovator With Improving Returns
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(TS_COUNT(xrd, 5), TREND(RATIO(ib, at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that report R&D continuously over five years and whose ROA is on a rising trend are converting a committed innovation program into realized earnings power.
evaluated.reasoning: Reporting persistence, not level, captures commitment to an innovation program, while the five-year ROA trend verifies that the program is actually paying off — neither channel alone distinguishes durable intangible productivity. The joint rank rewards sustained innovators with demonstrable profitability improvement and penalizes sporadic spenders and stagnant incumbents. This is a persistence-times-trajectory interaction that no single-theme variable can express.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self-Funded Knowledge Investment
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), at)), RANK(GROWTH(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cumulative R&D that is not accompanied by rising debt reflects internally financed, self-sustaining intangible investment; the same R&D funded by expanding leverage carries refinancing risk and is more likely to be cut.
evaluated.reasoning: The spread between intangible-investment rank and debt-growth rank isolates the financing quality of innovation, which is a balance-sheet dimension that R&D intensity alone ignores. High scorers accumulate knowledge capital while deleveraging or holding debt flat, a combination associated with resilient future earnings; low scorers are leverage-financed spenders vulnerable to credit shocks. The differencing form deliberately creates a novel funding-source interaction between the two themes.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Stock Meets Cash Coverage
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accumulated five-year R&D capital, not the single-year outlay, is the economically relevant intangible stock; its value is realized only where operating cash flow covers total liabilities, so debt-service capacity protects the knowledge base from forced disinvestment.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against the gen-0 winner — replacing the annual R&D flow with the cumulative knowledge stock — while holding the multiplicative rank interaction and the cash-coverage conditioner fixed. If the stock version improves both the FMB slope and the FF5 alpha, the mispricing is about un-capitalized intangible capital rather than about this year's spending decision. Unreported R&D is economically zero spending, justifying COALESCE.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Industry-Neutral Innovation On Cash Coverage
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: R&D intensity is overwhelmingly an industry attribute; within-industry relative innovation intensity, conditioned on firm-level cash coverage, is the part that carries information about durable intangible productivity rather than sector membership.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 winner may partly reflect a static tilt toward pharma/tech, which FF5 does not fully absorb and which makes portfolio composition unstable; industry-ranking the intangible leg removes that tilt and tests whether the interaction survives as a genuine firm-level effect. A comparable or higher t-alpha with a better Sharpe would indicate the mechanism is firm-specific; a collapse would tell us the effect is a sector bet. This is a clean, single-change diagnostic on the strongest archive result.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Continuous Goodwill-Accrual Overhang
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Acquired intangibles destroy value specifically where reported earnings run ahead of operating cash flow: such firms have bought growth that is validated only by accruals and face future impairments and earnings reversals.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the gen-0 failure, where the binary INDICATOR gate collapsed most firms to exactly zero and left an undefined long-short spread; replacing the gate with a continuous accrual rank produces a smoothly distributed score and well-populated extreme portfolios. The product is high only for firms that are jointly goodwill-heavy and accrual-heavy, which is the precise conditional the story requires. Firms reporting no goodwill genuinely carry zero acquired-intangible overhang.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Spending With Stable Cash Generation
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes intangible investment credible is the predictability of the cash flow funding it, not merely its level; firms combining heavy R&D plus advertising with low five-year cash-flow volatility can sustain intangible programs across the cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-0 tested intangible intensity against earnings (ib) volatility in an additive SUMRANK form and got a weak Sharpe of 0.118, whereas the multiplicative cash-level form scored 0.53 — this proposal separates the two confounded choices by using the multiplicative form with a cash-flow stability conditioner. Cash-flow volatility is less contaminated by accrual noise and one-off write-offs than ROA volatility, so it should be a cleaner measure of funding durability. Including advertising broadens the intangible base and improves coverage relative to R&D alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Mature Self-Financed Innovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Retained earnings relative to assets measures cumulative lifetime profitability and financial maturity; innovation undertaken by firms with a deep retained-earnings base is funded by proven past profits rather than by external capital or hope, and is therefore more likely to persist and pay off.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces a quality channel absent from the archive — the stock of historical profitability rather than current cash flow or earnings volatility — which separates seasoned innovators from cash-burning young R&D firms that dominate the high-R&D tail. Because negative retained earnings flag accumulated losses, the rank conditioner naturally short-circuits the intangible signal exactly where it is least credible. It also tests whether the winning interaction is about liquidity (oancf) or about accumulated profitability.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Unlevered Knowledge Investment
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible assets provide poor collateral, so leverage and knowledge investment are complements only in appearance; R&D-intensive firms with low debt burdens face no pressure to cut innovation in downturns and earn a durable productivity premium.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the failed Self-Funded Knowledge Investment signal, which differenced ranks (a form that already underperformed) and used noisy one-year debt growth with only 5.5% coverage; here the balance-sheet state is a stable leverage level and the combination is multiplicative, matching the archive's best-performing structure. The economic content is distinct from cash coverage: it is about debt-capacity fragility rather than current cash generation. Three-year cumulative R&D smooths lumpy program spending while retaining much broader coverage than five-year windows.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Funds-From-Operations Covered Innovation
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The credibility of R&D spending depends on internally generated funds available to service obligations; funds from operations (income before extraordinary items plus depreciation and amortization) measures the same debt-service capacity as operating cash flow but is available for far more firm-years.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a deliberate coverage repair of the archive's best mechanism — every strong variant is stuck at 9.1% coverage because of the `oancf` reporting window, and the FFO proxy should roughly double usable observations while keeping the economic content identical. If fmb_tstat and t-alpha hold up at higher coverage, we gain both statistical power and confidence that the result is not confined to a narrow post-1988 sample; if they degrade, we learn the accrual-free cash measure is essential rather than incidental.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Doubly Gated Knowledge Capital
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3), RATIO(re, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity requires both current cash-servicing capacity and a deep stock of accumulated past profits; the two quality conditioners capture flow and stock financial strength and should jointly discriminate credible knowledge capital better than either alone.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash coverage (fmb 4.94) and retained-earnings maturity (fmb 4.32) were the two best-performing conditioners in the archive but they measure distinct things — liquidity today versus proven lifetime profitability — so averaging their ranks inside the multiplicative gate should reduce conditioner noise without diluting the mechanism. This is a consolidation step, testing whether the quality leg is better represented as a composite state than as a single variable. The 5-year R&D stock is used because it marginally outperformed the annual flow in gen 1.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation With A Profitability Floor
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What protects an R&D program is not average profitability or low volatility but the worst-case earnings level: firms that stayed profitable even in their weakest of the last five years never face the distress that forces innovation budgets to be cut.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested cash-flow level, cash-flow volatility, retained earnings, and leverage as conditioners, but never a downside floor, which is the economically precise notion of "R&D that will not be abandoned." TS_MIN of ROA is a one-sided quality measure that treats upside variation as harmless, unlike VOL, which penalized firms whose earnings rose sharply and delivered only a 0.276 Sharpe. It is parsimonious and mechanically distinct from the mean-based conditioners already in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Capital Productivity Gated By Cash
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(xrd, 5))), 1)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The signal should reward intangible *productivity* — gross profit earned per dollar of accumulated knowledge and acquired intangible capital — rather than intangible *intensity*, with cash coverage confirming the profit is real.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive winner ranks firms on how much they spend on intangibles, which conflates commitment with waste; this proposal inverts the framing to ask how much gross profit the existing intangible base generates, which is the direct empirical counterpart of "durable intangible productivity." Because intensity and productivity are near-reciprocal constructions, the result is genuinely informative either way: a positive alpha means efficiency dominates, a null means the premium is compensation for committed spending rather than realized output. Winsorization controls the small-denominator tail among light R&D reporters.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Under Low Debt Service Burden
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), ADD(ib, dp)), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What threatens intangible programs is not the leverage ratio itself but the number of years of cash earnings required to repay debt; low debt-to-FFO means creditors exert no pressure to cut discretionary innovation spending.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs Unlevered Knowledge Investment, whose leverage-to-assets conditioner produced a strong t-alpha (3.83) but a near-zero FMB slope (0.58), a signature of a highly non-monotone score in which only the extremes carry information. Debt relative to cash earnings orders firms by an economically continuous distress-proximity scale and should restore a monotone cross-sectional slope while preserving the portfolio-level effect. Winsorization is necessary because the ratio explodes when FFO approaches zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Ramp From A Profitable Base
evaluated.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, at), 5), RANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm escalating R&D intensity relative to its own five-year history is signalling private optimism about its opportunity set; that signal is credible only when the firm's own recent profitability is high enough to fund the escalation without external capital.
evaluated.reasoning: All archive signals score the intangible leg on a cross-sectional level, which is dominated by permanent industry and business-model differences; own-history position isolates the firm's innovation decision at the margin and is a genuinely different information channel. Interacting the ramp with sustained profitability separates confident, self-funded expansion from desperate spending by deteriorating firms, which is exactly the credibility condition in the economic story. Raw `xrd` is used so the own-history rank is computed only for genuine, continuous R&D reporters rather than degenerating to ties at zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Gated By Cash Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The credibility gate on R&D may be simple cash profitability (cash flow per dollar of assets) rather than solvency-style coverage of total liabilities; if so, the mechanism is about the productivity of the asset base funding innovation, not about creditor pressure.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best signals all scale operating cash flow by total liabilities, which mixes a profitability signal with an inverse-leverage signal, and the separate leverage experiments showed that the leverage component is non-monotone and FMB-invisible. Rescaling by assets isolates the pure cash-profitability content of the gate at identical coverage, so a comparison with Cash-Covered Innovation Intensity cleanly attributes the 4.6% alpha to profitability or to solvency. This is a one-variable diagnostic on the most important open question in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash Coverage With Accounting Fallback
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating cash flow is the economically correct coverage measure, but where the cash-flow statement is unavailable, funds from operations is its closest accounting reconstruction; using it only as a fallback preserves the strong mechanism while extending the sample.
evaluated.reasoning: Gen-2 showed that wholesale substitution of FFO for `oancf` bought coverage at a real cost in alpha and Sharpe, implying the true cash measure carries information that accruals destroy — but that is an argument for a hierarchical measurement convention, not for discarding the extra firm-years. COALESCE here encodes a defensible reporting convention (use reported cash flow; reconstruct it only when absent) rather than a blanket coverage patch. If alpha and t-alpha stay near the 4.6%/3.2 benchmark at roughly 14% coverage, this becomes the preferred consolidation base for later generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Minus Acquired Intangibles On Cash
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Internally generated knowledge capital and purchased intangibles have opposite return implications: the former is unrecorded and underpriced, the latter is recorded at acquisition cost and prone to impairment, so the intangible *mix* conditioned on cash quality is a sharper signal than intangible level.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive contains direct evidence for this asymmetry — organic R&D stocks gated by cash earn +4.6% alpha while goodwill-heavy accrual firms earn −3.4% — but no signal has yet exploited both sides in one score. Differencing the two intangible ranks before the cash gate builds a long-organic/short-acquired intangible portfolio among firms that all pass the same financial-strength filter, isolating the composition effect from the level effect. Both factors are bounded ranks, so the product stays monotone and avoids the sign pathologies of raw differencing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation With Conservative Accruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The relevant quality condition is that reported earnings are backed by cash rather than accruals: an R&D-intensive firm whose profits convert into cash is genuinely funding innovation, while one whose profits are accrual-driven is capitalizing optimism twice.
evaluated.reasoning: Every successful gate so far measures the *level* of cash generation; this one measures its *quality* relative to reported earnings, which is a distinct construct and is exactly the accounting condition that separates credible from cosmetic profitability. It also completes a natural pair with the goodwill-accrual result, testing whether low accruals help innovators as much as high accruals hurt acquirers. Coverage matches the archive's cash-based signals, so results are directly comparable to the 4.6% benchmark.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Acquired Intangible Overhang Without Cash
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles are a liability rather than an asset when the acquirer lacks cash coverage: such firms have levered up to buy growth they cannot service, and face impairments, dilution, and forced divestiture.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior goodwill signal used an accrual conditioner and produced a reliable portfolio effect (−3.4%, t = −2.17) but no cross-sectional slope; replacing the accrual gate with the same cash-coverage gate that powers the archive's best long signal tests whether the mechanism is symmetric and should generate a monotone score across the whole cross-section. Broadening the intangible leg from goodwill alone to all balance-sheet intangibles increases the number of firms with non-zero exposure, which should further reduce the mass-at-zero problem that produced the gen-0 degenerate portfolio. A clean short leg is valuable in its own right and could be combined with the long mechanism later.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Triple-Gated Durable Innovator
evaluated.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity requires innovation intensity, current cash-servicing capacity, and a demonstrated floor under profitability; only firms clearing all three conditions have knowledge capital that survives a full cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash coverage (alpha 4.6%, Sharpe 0.55) and the five-year worst-case ROA floor (alpha 3.9%, t 3.60) are the two best-performing gates and they measure different things — liquidity now versus resilience in the trough — yet gen-2 showed that averaging conditioners with SUMRANK dilutes the signal. Multiplicative stacking preserves the conjunctive logic, keeping the score near zero unless every condition is met, which should concentrate the extreme portfolios on the intended firms. This directly tests whether the archive's conditioners are substitutes or complements, a decision needed before consolidating in later generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Mix On Cash Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Organic knowledge capital is underpriced and purchased intangibles are overpriced; the spread between them, conditioned on the firm's cash productivity of assets, isolates durable intangible productivity.
evaluated.reasoning: This combines the two independent gen-3 improvements — the organic-minus-acquired mix (alpha 6.6%, t 4.59) and the asset-scaled cash gate, which beat the liability-scaled gate on alpha, t-alpha and Sharpe when tested on a fixed intangible leg. Because each change was validated separately on the same 9.1% sample, their combination is the natural consolidation point and is directly comparable to both parents. If both effects are additive, this should be the archive's strongest signal on all four metrics simultaneously.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Mix With Cash Fallback Gate
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The mix mechanism should hold across the full sample, not only in the post-cash-flow-statement era; reconstructing cash flow from funds from operations where it is unreported extends the test without changing the economics.
evaluated.reasoning: Every top signal is capped at 9.1% coverage purely because of `oancf` availability, and the gen-3 fallback test showed the convention preserves a strong slope (fmb 4.76) at 14.2% coverage though with some alpha decay. Applying the fallback to the far stronger mix signal tests whether the alpha decay was a property of the weak intangible leg or of the measurement substitution itself. A durable 5%-plus alpha at 14% coverage would be more investable than a 6.6% alpha on a third fewer observations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Organic Share Of Intangible Capital
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the composition of a firm's intangible base — the fraction built internally rather than bought — because internally built capital reflects demonstrated innovation capability while purchased capital reflects a price paid to someone else.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-3 mix signal used a difference of two cross-sectional ranks, which is scale-free but conflates a firm with large offsetting intangible positions with one that has almost none; a within-firm share cleanly measures composition and is invariant to overall intangible size. Comparing this ratio construction against Signal 1's rank-difference construction on the same gate tells us whether the alpha comes from intangible *composition* or from being simultaneously high-R&D and low-goodwill. Firms with neither R&D nor recorded intangibles are legitimately undefined here, which keeps the score interpretable.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Mix With Profitability Floor
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The intangible-mix premium requires only that the firm's profitability never collapsed; a five-year worst-case ROA floor is a sufficient credibility condition and is measurable for far more firms than operating cash flow.
evaluated.reasoning: This substitutes the gate while holding the now-dominant intangible leg fixed, which separates the contribution of the mix from the contribution of the specific cash conditioner and simultaneously raises coverage to roughly 14.6%. The profitability floor was the best-performing wide-coverage gate in gen 2 (alpha 3.9%, t 3.60) despite a weak intangible leg, so pairing it with the strong leg is the highest-expected-value coverage experiment available. If alpha approaches the cash-gated version, the mechanism is robustly about intangible composition rather than about liquidity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Acquisitive Expansion Without Cash Support
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), 1), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Recent goodwill additions — the flow of acquisitions — signal empire-building when made by firms with weak cash productivity, and predict subsequent impairments and negative abnormal returns more sharply than the accumulated goodwill stock.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's short leg so far uses the intangible *stock*, which is stale and reflects deals made many years ago; the annual change isolates the current management decision and should be more timely about impairment risk. Scaling the change by assets keeps it comparable across firm size, and pairing it with the same cash gate that powers the long side tests whether the timing of bad acquisitions is priced with a lag. This is a distinct economic channel — acquisition flow rather than intangible level — on the side of the trade where the archive already has reliable evidence.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Long Organic Short Acquired Composite
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))), RANK(MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two validated mechanisms — cash-backed organic innovation earning positive alpha and cash-starved acquired intangibles earning negative alpha — are economically distinct and should be combined into a single score rather than traded separately.
evaluated.reasoning: Signal 1 imposes a single common gate on a differenced intangible leg, which forces both sides to share the same conditioner; this construction instead builds each leg with its own economically correct gate (high cash for organic innovators, low cash for acquirers) and then differences the resulting ranks. Given the parents delivered +6.6% and −5.6% alpha with t-statistics above 4 in absolute value, an imperfectly correlated combination should raise both t-alpha and Sharpe even if the alpha magnitude sits between the two. Differencing ranks rather than raw scores keeps the composite bounded and avoids the scale pathologies that sank the gen-0 rank-difference attempt.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Mix With Full Acquired Intangible Leg
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Goodwill is the most impairment-prone component of purchased intangibles, so weighting it explicitly alongside other recorded intangibles should sharpen the short side of the mix.
evaluated.reasoning: The best long signal uses `intan` alone on the acquired leg, while the best short signal used `gdwl + intan` and produced −5.6% alpha with t = −4.02, so double-weighting goodwill within the recorded intangible base is the single most promising untested leg refinement. This is a one-variable change against the reigning benchmark, making attribution unambiguous. If it improves alpha and t-alpha, later generations should keep goodwill explicitly weighted.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Brand And Knowledge Capital Mix
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Advertising builds brand capital that is expensed exactly like R&D and equally invisible on the balance sheet; the organic intangible leg should therefore include accumulated advertising, not only research.
evaluated.reasoning: The organic leg is currently R&D-only, which mechanically excludes consumer-facing firms whose internally built intangible is brand rather than patents, and gen-0/gen-1 evidence showed adding `xad` broadened coverage without breaking the effect. Testing this alone, with the acquired leg and gate unchanged, determines whether the premium is specific to technological knowledge or general to self-created intangible capital. A gain here would materially widen the investable universe of the winning mechanism.

evaluated.name: Mix Penalized By Acquisition Flow

evaluated.hypothesis: Both the stock of purchased intangibles and the current-year flow of new acquisitions detract from intangible credibility, and the flow adds timely information about management's present capital-allocation choice.

evaluated.name: Industry-Neutral Intangible Mix
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the mix premium is a firm-level effect, it should survive ranking within industry; if it is mostly a structural long-technology/short-serial-acquirer sector bet, industry-neutralization will remove it.
evaluated.reasoning: R&D intensity and goodwill intensity are strongly and oppositely determined by industry, so the 6.5% alpha may partly be a persistent sector tilt that FF5 does not span and that would make portfolio composition static and crowded. The analogous gen-1 test on the simple R&D leg cost only modest performance (alpha 4.6% → 4.0%), suggesting a firm-level core exists; running it on the far stronger mix leg is the decisive version of the test. A robust result here materially raises confidence in the mechanism ahead of final consolidation.

evaluated.name: Weakest-Link Cash Durability Gate
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible intangible investment requires cash flow that is both high and dependable; the binding constraint is whichever condition is weaker, so the gate should be the minimum of the two ranks rather than their average or product.
evaluated.reasoning: Every previous attempt to combine two quality conditions used SUMRANK averaging, which diluted the signal (Doubly Gated: alpha 3.0%), or triple multiplication, which also underperformed; MIN implements a genuine weakest-link conjunction and is a structurally new way to express the credibility condition. Cash-flow level and cash-flow stability are conceptually independent — a firm can be highly profitable but erratic — and the story explicitly requires both. If MIN beats the level-only gate, the credibility condition is conjunctive and later refinements should use it.

evaluated.name: Intangible Mix On Improving Cash Productivity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge capital is validated by a rising path of cash productivity, not merely a high level: an improving trend is the observable evidence that past intangible investment is currently converting into cash.
evaluated.reasoning: All successful gates to date measure the level or floor of profitability, which tends to select mature, already-recognized firms; a five-year trend identifies firms where the intangible payoff is arriving now and is most likely to be under-extrapolated by investors. Trend-based quality already showed promise in gen 0 (t-alpha 3.67) despite a crude intangible leg, so pairing it with the dominant mix leg is the natural test of trajectory versus level. It is also economically the closest expression of "durable intangible productivity" as a realized outcome rather than a funding precondition.

evaluated.name: Asset-Light Knowledge Mix On Cash
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)))), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge capital should be measured relative to the tangible asset base it complements: a firm with a large research stock per dollar of hard assets is genuinely asset-light and its economic capital is most severely understated by accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: Every version to date scales the organic leg by total assets, which already contains recorded intangibles and therefore mechanically shrinks the organic score for exactly the acquisitive firms the signal wants to short, muddying the contrast between the two legs. Netting recorded intangibles out of the denominator makes the two legs cleanly orthogonal in construction — hidden capital per tangible dollar versus recorded intangibles per total dollar — and should widen the spread between the poles. The denominator stays positive for essentially all firms, so no rank pathologies are introduced.

evaluated.name: Mix Gated By Cash Level And Accrual Quality
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible investment is credible only if the firm both generates substantial cash and reports earnings that are backed by that cash; the binding condition is whichever of the two is weaker.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash level and accrual quality were separately validated as gates (alpha 5.3% and 5.7%, t-alpha 3.72 and 3.80) and are conceptually distinct — one is magnitude, the other is the earnings-to-cash reconciliation — while MIN was the only combination operator that preserved alpha in gen 5. This is the highest-expected-value stacking experiment remaining because the accrual gate's weak FMB slope (1.71) should be repaired by pairing it with a monotone cash-level rank inside MIN. If it clears the 6.5% benchmark on both alpha and t-alpha it becomes the consolidation candidate.

evaluated.name: Goodwill At Risk To Equity Without Cash

evaluated.hypothesis: Impairment risk is best measured against the equity it would destroy, not against total assets: when purchased intangibles exceed book equity and cash generation is weak, a write-down mechanically wipes out the shareholders' stated claim.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's short leg (alpha −5.6%, t −4.02) scales acquired intangibles by assets, which understates vulnerability for levered roll-ups whose equity is thin relative to the goodwill they carry; equity scaling is the standard solvency-relevant framing of impairment exposure. Because the long side of the trade is already strong, improving the short pole is the most direct route to a higher combined alpha in the final generations. Cash productivity is retained as the conditioner so results are directly comparable with the existing short signal.

evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5)), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The full stock of self-created intangibles — research plus brand — is credible when cash generation is simultaneously high and stable, so both the intangible leg and the gate should be broadened to their validated best forms.

evaluated.name: Innovation Budget Covered By Cash Flow
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), MA(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically exact credibility test is whether operating cash flow covers the intangible spending program itself: a firm whose cash flow is several times its annual R&D and advertising budget can sustain that program indefinitely without external finance.
evaluated.reasoning: All gates so far scale cash flow by an accounting base (assets, liabilities) that is unrelated to the intangible commitment being funded, whereas this ratio measures coverage of the actual outlay, which is what determines whether a program gets cut. It also creates informative tension with the long leg — heavy spenders need very strong cash flow to score well — so the signal selects firms with high intangible intensity *and* headroom, rather than either alone. Winsorization is required because the coverage ratio explodes for firms with negligible intangible budgets.

evaluated.name: Two-Pole Intangible Credibility Composite
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5)), at)), MIN(RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))))), RANK(MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ceq)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))))))

Unlike Signal 4, which forces one shared conditioner onto a differenced intangible leg, this construction lets each side use the conditioner its own economics implies, which is why the two designs are worth carrying forward in parallel. evaluated.reasoning: The earnings-based floor (TS_MIN of ROA) preserved t-alpha but collapsed the Sharpe to 0.169, which I attribute to accounting write-offs and one-off charges contaminating the minimum of `ib`; the same construct built on operating cash flow should be far cleaner because cash flow is immune to non-cash charges. This is the one gate concept — a one-sided cash durability floor — that the archive has never tested, and it distinguishes "never weak" from "high on average" (MA) and "not volatile" (VOL). If it beats the MA gate, the mechanism is about downside resilience rather than average strength.

Pairing it with the proven cash gate inside MIN gives the balance-sheet channel its fairest test within the structure that is known to work. evaluated.hypothesis: The right measure of acquired-intangible burden is how many years of operating cash flow the purchase price represents; a firm carrying ten years of cash flow in goodwill has paid for growth it may never deliver.
